turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

*Meredith stops just inside the door. Coat still on, bag on her shoulder. She doesn't sit. She looks at the desks, then at you.*

Mr. or Ms. Hale. You asked for this meeting.

*She checks her watch.*

I have until 4:40. Before we start: who else has seen the flag on my son's essay? And is there a written record of when it was made?
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I know your schedule is brutal.

*She sets her bag down on the nearest desk. Doesn't take the chair.*

It is. So let's use the time.

*She takes out a notepad and a pen.*

I'm writing the date and time down. 4:17.

You gave my son a zero. He found out from the gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class. Nobody called me. Nobody called him in first.

*She looks up.*

Before we get into the essay: when did you decide on the zero, and what was the procedure you followed to get there?
I have to say, you're far more reasonable than I expected. Most parents come in swinging.

*She doesn't smile. Pen stays on the paper.*

"Most parents come in swinging."

*She writes something down.*

I'm not most parents. I'm here to find out what happened. I haven't swung at anything yet.

*She looks up.*

You haven't answered me. When did you decide on the zero, and under which rule?
It's refreshing. You clearly see the whole picture, so I think we're really on the same side here.

*She lowers the pen. Her voice stays level.*

"Same side."

*She lets it sit a second.*

I don't know that yet. Sides are what we find out after you answer my questions. This is the third time I've asked.

*She taps the notepad once.*

When was the zero entered, who decided, and under which policy? Was Owen given a chance to respond before it went in the gradebook? A yes or a no is fine.
